verdict.rationale: Conductor's docs explicitly describe cloud workspaces where 'agents keep working after you close your laptop' and sandboxes 'spin up in seconds' (conductor-docs-20), agents can run tests/builds without confirmation (conductor-docs-17), and tasks can run scheduled via 'routines' or GitHub Actions (conductor-docs-4), plus API/MCP control of cloud workspaces (conductor-docs-13, conductor-docs-14). This directly matches delegating longer-running background tasks to an isolated cloud environment. A community note (conductor-comm-17) clarifies that the default mode uses local git worktrees while cloud containers are a separate opt-in mode, slightly muddying which mode is default, but does not contradict that the isolated cloud capability exists and works. Missing for 10: independent hands-on verification of cloud sandbox isolation/security and clearer default-mode framing.
